video_title: This SUPER FAST 2.0 Log Bait Cycle is BUSTED!!

I swear it has way too much HP. It has more HP than a giant literally." The only matching observation is a `skeleton-king-skill` ability detection on the opponent's side at clock 1:57, so this is probably the Skeleton King, but the transcript name and the HP claim do not line up cleanly and no Skeleton King body was ever detected.

bullets: Game 2 of 7 in the video (170.3s-342.3s), a win against an off-meta Royal Recruits / Bowler / Skeleton Barrel control deck. Ryley chips with Goblin Barrels and Dart Goblins for the first minute and only commits once, at clock 1:38-1:30 (Dart Goblin + Wall Breakers + Evolution Goblin Barrel + Berserker), which takes the enemy left tower from 4858 to 1160 HP.

The deck's damage pattern here is a 5-elixir bridge package rather than a single win condition: Berserker at (15, 15) plus Goblin Barrel at (14, 25) plus Wall Breakers, run at clock 2:13-2:02 and again at clock 0:20-0:07. Both times the opponent's answer was too slow and the tower dropped by roughly 1,300 HP.

The Cannon is treated as a reserved resource, not a cycle card: he holds it through a Bowler counter-push at clock 1:12-1:10 ("I'm going to save my cannon because of the Skeleton Barrel ... I'd rather just take the Bowler shot") and again at clock 0:44, and only pre-places it at clock 0:28 when he expects Royal Recruits at the bridge.

The Goblin Barrel doubles as spell bait, and the deck's line is barrel-first-then-Dart-Goblin: "Barrel here to try to force out the Arrows. Then we can go for the Dark Goblin off to the side" (289-292s). Both late barrels went into the lane away from the Royal Recruits.

Stated weakness (229-241s): "you can tell the spirits are a decent amount worse whenever you're defending a card like Archer Queen or Musketeer because the Musketeer and the Archer Queen one-shotting spirits does actually make defense very difficult in quite a few scenarios." Against a deck without those cards the 1-elixir spirits carried the whole defence, including the Royal Recruits push at clock 0:44.

Confidence note: the video-level consensus deck (all 7 games) matched this game's per-game read exactly, but the HUD hand confidence is only 0.576 and several plays were recovered from deploy labels and commentary instead (see the match file's Data gaps).

new_deck.rationale: Ryley's own title for it is "this SUPER FAST 2.0 Log Bait Cycle": Goblin Barrel, Skeletons and Dart Goblin exist to pull the small spell, and at exactly 2.0 average elixir the deck wins by cycling back to the barrel faster than the answer.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: Every card is 1-3 elixir, so the deck never has to choose between defending and threatening: in this match Ryley answered a Zappies push, a Bowler counter-push and a six-body Royal Recruits push with Skeletons, Ice Spirit and Electro Spirit alone, and still threw five Goblin Barrels. Damage comes from repetition rather than one big push — a 5-elixir Berserker + Goblin Barrel + Wall Breakers package at the bridge, run whenever the opponent's answer is out of cycle, took roughly 1,300 HP off a tower each time it landed. The Goblin Barrel's second job is spell bait ("Barrel here to try to force out the Arrows. Then we can go for the Dark Goblin off to the side"), and the Dart Goblin is the card that cashes in once the spell is gone, played off to the side of the arena to stay out of splash. The Cannon is the only defensive anchor and is deliberately hoarded for the one card that would otherwise punish the deck — here the Evolution Skeleton Barrel — which means the deck accepts chip damage from anything the cheap troops can survive. Its stated soft spot is a defender that one-shots spirits: "the spirits are a decent amount worse whenever you're defending a card like Archer Queen or Musketeer."
